findings.summary: ACM Queue is a bimonthly electronic trade magazine for practicing software engineers, published by the Association for Computing Machinery since 2003. It bridges academic and industrial computer science, featuring research articles, columns, and interviews. Unlike peer-reviewed journals, publication requires invitation and review but is not formally peer-reviewed. Content is editorially curated and available by subscription.

mechanisms.title: Editorial selection process
mechanisms.explanation: Only articles from specifically invited authors undergo a review process before publication, distinguishing it from open academic journals.

mechanisms.title: Content format and distribution
mechanisms.explanation: The magazine publishes research articles, columns, and interviews in electronic form, with some content cross-published in ACM's Communications magazine Practitioner section.
